detail.body:
# AutoEP: support `combine_impl="fused_weighted_sum"` with AutoEP+AutoTP folding

<!-- r3 2026-10-15. Branch peng-autoep-fused-combine-folded-tp-v2 (worktree /fsx/peng/workspace/ds-autoep-fused-combine-folded-tp-v2) on master 5f266e26d, not committed. The fork has peng-autoep-fused-combine-folded-tp-v1 (2f7ee8758, never opened as a PR); this branch is the same change on master 5f266e26d (3 hunks apply with line offsets). -->

**Part of:** #8672 (Q4 2026 roadmap), "Mixture-of-Expert (MoE) Training Scaling and Kernel Development": "AutoEP Performance Optimization & Parallel Folding (AutoEP + AutoTP)" (PoC @tohtana @pengdurice). Follows #8670.

## Problem

`combine_impl="fused_weighted_sum"` was refused whenever `tensor_parallel.autotp_size > 1`:

- `deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_config.py` (`validate_autoep_config`) raised `ValueError`.
- `deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_layer.py` (`set_deepspeed_parallelism`) raised the same error.

The reason was that the folded path restores tokens with its own function, `restore_combined` in
`deepspeed/moe/ep_tp_dispatch.py`, and the fused kernel was only wired into the unfolded path.

`restore_combined` works like this:

1. Each TP peer sends only part of the routed assignments to the experts (`partition_assignments`).
2. After the experts, it all-gathers the rows, their token index, their top-k slot and their routing weight over the
   TP group.
3. It casts the routing weights to the activation dtype, multiplies, and adds the products with one `index_add_` per
   top-k slot, all in the activation dtype.

So under folding, users could not get the memory saving and the FP32 accumulation of the fused kernel, and the
folded restore did its arithmetic in bf16.

## Change

- New `restore_combined_fused` in `deepspeed/moe/ep_tp_dispatch.py`:
  - It does the same differentiable all-gathers as `restore_combined` for the rows and the routing weights, so the
    `tp_size` gradient factor that the folded AVERAGE and EXPERT_TP_CANCEL strategies cancel is unchanged.
  - It all-gathers one flat index (`token * top_k + slot`) instead of the token index and the slot separately.
  - It keeps the routing weights in the router dtype, scatters them into `[tokens, top_k]`, and calls the existing
    `fused_weighted_restore`. The kernel is unchanged.
  - It raises a clear `RuntimeError` if the gathered rows do not cover every (token, slot). The folded payload never
    drops or pads assignments today, so this cannot trigger now; it protects the kernel from reading an unset source
    row if capacity dropping is added later.
  - `validate_coverage=True` runs the same coverage check as `restore_combined`.
- `AutoEPMoELayer._forward` calls `restore_combined_fused` in the folded branch when
  `combine_impl == "fused_weighted_sum"`. The default (`"auto"` → `"weighted_sum"`) still calls `restore_combined`.
- The two `autotp_size > 1` refusals are removed. The other fused refusals stay: `expert_tensor_parallel_size > 1`,
  DeepEP, `score_apply` other than `"post"`, and unsupported device or dtype.
- Docs: `docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst` describes the folded fused restore and drops the refusal from the list;
  `docs/_pages/config-json.md` drops the `autotp_size=1` requirement.

## Tests

All GPU runs: one node of 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs. torch 2.8.0+cu126 with Triton 3.4.0, and torch 2.9.1+cu128 with Triton 3.5.1.

| Test | What it checks | GPUs | torch 2.8.0 | torch 2.9.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test_autoep_unit.py::TestAutoEPConfig::test_fused_combine_accepts_folded_tensor_parallelism` (was `..._rejects_...`) | the config is accepted with `tp_size=2` | 0 | passed | not run |
| `test_autoep_autotp_dispatch.py::test_restore_combined_fused_rejects_a_missing_assignment` | a missing (token, slot) raises instead of reading an unset row | 0 | passed | passed |
| `test_autoep_autotp_dispatch.py::TestRestoreCombinedFusedTensorParallel` (fp32 and bf16 rows) | 2 TP peers with different row counts, each back-propagating a different gradient: the output is bitwise equal to the unpartitioned `fused_weighted_restore`, and the row and score gradients, summed over the peers, match the unpartitioned gradients | 2 | 2 passed | 2 passed |
| `test_autoep_fused_parity.py::TestAutoEPFusedParityFoldedTensorParallel` (ZeRO 0 and 2, with and without activation checkpointing) | one training step with TP 2 × EP 2: the loss, output, input gradient, every parameter gradient and every parameter update of the fused run match the default folded run | 4 | 4 passed | 4 passed |
| Rest of `test_autoep_autotp_dispatch.py` | no change to `restore_combined` | 0 | 9 passed | 9 passed |
| `test_autoep_fused_token_ops.py` | the kernel is unchanged | 1 | 63 passed | not run |
| `test_autoep_autotp_grad_parity.py` with `DEEPSPEED_RUN_H100_TESTS=1` | no change to the default folded path | up to 8 | 22 passed | not run |
| Whole `test_autoep_unit.py` | no other config change | up to 8 | 198 passed (master: 198 passed) | not run |

Rerun on master `d371f33cc` with this change (torch 2.8.0+cu126): `test_autoep_autotp_dispatch.py` 12
passed; `test_autoep_fused_parity.py` 4 passed (the 4 new folded cases) and 3 failed; `test_autoep_unit.py` 198 passed.
The 3 failures are existing cases (`TestAutoEPFusedParityExpertParallel` x 2, `TestAutoEPFusedParityLocalExperts`) and
fail the same on master without this change: "Expected mat_a to be BFloat16 matrix got Half", torch 2.8's
`_grouped_mm` takes bf16 only and these cases run in fp16.

The end-to-end folded test runs in FP32, on `MockMoEOnlyTransformer`, without grouped GEMM:

- FP32: the default folded restore rounds each product and each top-k addition to the activation dtype. In fp16 the
  two restores differ by 1 to 1.5 units in the last place of the MoE output (about 1,600 in this model), which is more
  than `PARITY_TOLERANCE` allows after the LM head. In FP32 the two forward passes are bitwise equal.
- No attention: the key bias of `nn.MultiheadAttention` has a true gradient of zero, so its computed gradient is
  rounding noise, and Adam's first step turns that noise into ±lr. The parameter-update check then fails by 2 × lr no
  matter which restore is used.
- No grouped GEMM: on torch 2.8, `torch._grouped_mm` accepts only bf16, so the fp32 run would fail before reaching the
  restore.

Existing tests in `test_autoep_fused_parity.py` that fail on master `c6af3faf2` in this environment, before this change
(not changed here):

- torch 2.8.0: all 3 fail with `RuntimeError: Expected mat_a to be BFloat16 matrix got Half`. The tests use fp16 and
  the default grouped GEMM.
- torch 2.9.1: `TestAutoEPFusedParityExpertParallel` (2 cases) fails on the input gradient: 5 of 1,024 elements, with
  the largest relative difference 2.1% against a 1% limit. Under fp16 the input gradient still carries the loss scale
  of 256. `TestAutoEPFusedParityLocalExperts` passes.


On master 5f266e26d (2026-10-15; 1 node of 8 H200, driver 580.126.09, torch 2.8.0+cu126): 214 passed, 3 failed: the 3 fp16 cases of `test_autoep_fused_parity.py` (`TestAutoEPFusedParityExpertParallel` x2, `TestAutoEPFusedParityLocalExperts`: torch 2.8 `_grouped_mm` takes bf16 only), which fail the same way on master 5f266e26d without this change.
Failures that also fail on master are rerun on master in the same job.

## Benchmark

One TP group of 2 H200 GPUs on one node. bf16 rows, FP32 routing weights, random routing with distinct experts per
token. The hidden size, top-k and expert count are the MiniMax-M3 and GLM-5.2 values. Memory is the peak above the
inputs. Time is one forward and backward, averaged over 10 runs after 3 warm-up runs, and includes the identical
partition step. Errors are against an FP64 reference.

| Shape (tokens per TP group, top-k, experts, hidden) | Forward peak, GiB (default → fused) | Backward peak, GiB | Time, ms | Output error, relative L2 | Score gradient error, relative L2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8,192, 4, 128, 6144 (MiniMax-M3) | 1.22 → 0.75 | 1.59 → 0.84 | 13.3 → 7.4 | 3.58e-3 → 1.66e-3 | 2.35e-3 → 8.4e-8 |
| 32,768, 4, 128, 6144 (MiniMax-M3) | 4.88 → 3.00 | 6.38 → 3.38 | 41.1 → 21.0 | 3.57e-3 → 1.66e-3 | 2.34e-3 → 8.3e-8 |
| 8,192, 8, 256, 6144 (GLM-5.2) | 2.35 → 1.50 | 3.09 → 1.60 | 26.7 → 12.0 | 4.36e-3 → 1.66e-3 | 2.34e-3 → 8.6e-8 |
| 32,768, 8, 256, 6144 (GLM-5.2) | 9.39 → 6.01 | 12.38 → 6.38 | 91.9 → 38.8 | 4.36e-3 → 1.66e-3 | 2.35e-3 → 8.7e-8 |

The fused output error of 1.66e-3 is the rounding of the bf16 output itself. The score gradient is the router
gradient; the default folded path computes it through bf16 weights, the fused path in FP32.

Script: `bench_folded_restore.py` (run with `torchrun --nproc_per_node=2`).

## Notes

- The default folded path and the fused path give close but not bitwise-equal results, because the default path
  multiplies and adds in the activation dtype.
- AutoEP+AutoTP folding with ZeRO-3 is still refused on master; this change does not alter that.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and recent pull requests on 2026-10-15 ("fused_weighted_sum", "combine", "folding", "AutoEP + AutoTP"): none enables the fused combine under folding. #8829 (optimizer offload under folding) and #8823 (ZeRO-1/2 clipping under folding) change other parts of folding; #8745 and #8739 change the DeepEP combine.

## Proposal

New functionality: per CONTRIBUTING.md it needs an accepted proposal issue first. Draft:
`descriptions/r3/peng-autoep-fused-combine-folded-tp-v2-proposal-issue.md`. TODO(user): open the issue, wait for acceptance, then link it here.

## AI assistance

This change, its tests and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude).

@@ -482,5 +482,68 @@ def restore_combined(local_combined: torch.Tensor,
     return output
 
 
+def restore_combined_fused(local_combined: torch.Tensor,
+                           ctx: RestoreContext,
+                           *,
+                           tp_group,
+                           top_k: int,
+                           validate_coverage: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``restore_combined`` with the weighted top-k reduction done by the fused kernel.
+
+    The rows and the routing weights go through the same differentiable
+    all-gather as ``restore_combined``, so the ``tp_size`` gradient factor that
+    the folded AVERAGE and EXPERT_TP_CANCEL strategies cancel is unchanged. Only
+    the reduction differs: ``fused_weighted_restore`` multiplies each row by its
+    FP32 score and adds a token's top-k products in slot order in FP32, without
+    the reduced-precision product and the per-slot ``index_add_``.
+    """
+    from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops import autoep_fused_token_ops as fused_token_ops
+
+    payload = ctx.original_payload
+    local_token_indices = payload.token_indices.index_select(0, ctx.local_indices)
+    local_capacity_slots = payload.capacity_slots.index_select(0, ctx.local_indices)
+    # Position of each row in the unpartitioned [tokens * top_k] assignment order.
+    local_flat_indices = local_token_indices * top_k + local_capacity_slots
+    # Keep the router dtype: the kernel applies the scores in FP32.
+    local_weights = payload.combine_weights.index_select(0, ctx.local_indices)
+
+    all_outputs = _all_gather_variable_rows(local_combined,
+                                            tp_group,
+                                            ctx.tp_size,
+                                            preserve_grad=local_combined.requires_grad)
+    all_flat_indices = _all_gather_variable_rows(local_flat_indices, tp_group, ctx.tp_size).to(torch.long)
+    all_weights = _all_gather_variable_rows(local_weights,
+                                            tp_group,
+                                            ctx.tp_size,
+                                            preserve_grad=local_weights.requires_grad)
+    if validate_coverage:
+        local_expert_indices = payload.expert_indices.index_select(0, ctx.local_indices)
+        local_assignment_indices = payload.assignment_indices.index_select(0, ctx.local_indices)
+        all_expert_indices = _all_gather_variable_rows(local_expert_indices, tp_group, ctx.tp_size).to(torch.long)
+        all_assignment_indices = _all_gather_variable_rows(local_assignment_indices, tp_group,
+                                                           ctx.tp_size).to(torch.long)
+        _debug_validate_restore_coverage(payload, ctx, all_flat_indices // top_k, all_expert_indices,
+                                         all_assignment_indices, all_flat_indices % top_k)
+
+    if ctx.num_tokens <= 0:
+        ctx.num_tokens = int(payload.token_indices.max().item()) + 1 if payload.token_indices.numel() else 0
+    num_assignments = ctx.num_tokens * top_k
+    # The kernel reads one row for every (token, slot), so a dropped or padded
+    # assignment would leave its source row unset instead of contributing zero.
+    if all_outputs.shape[0] != num_assignments:
+        raise RuntimeError('combine_impl="fused_weighted_sum" needs every (token, top-k slot) assignment after the '
+                           f"AutoEP+AutoTP restore, but gathered {all_outputs.shape[0]} rows for "
+                           f"{ctx.num_tokens} tokens x top_k={top_k}. Leave combine_impl unset.")
+
+    top_scores = all_weights.new_zeros(num_assignments).scatter(0, all_flat_indices, all_weights)
+    hidden = local_combined.shape[-1]
+    output = fused_token_ops.fused_weighted_restore(all_outputs,
+                                                    top_scores=top_scores.view(ctx.num_tokens, top_k),
+                                                    token_indices_sorted=all_flat_indices,
+                                                    top_k=top_k,
+                                                    shape=(1, ctx.num_tokens, hidden))
+    return output.reshape(ctx.num_tokens, hidden)
+
+
 def dispatch_counters(ctx: RestoreContext) -> dict[str, int]:
     return dict(ctx.counters)

+def test_restore_combined_fused_rejects_a_missing_assignment():
+    payload, _, _ = _tp_payload_for_backward_parity()
+    _, ctx = partition_assignments(payload, tp_group=None, tp_rank=0, tp_size=1)

+def _fused_restore_available():
+    accelerator = get_accelerator()
+    return accelerator.is_available() and accelerator.device_name().startswith("cuda") and fused_ops.is_available()

+
+def _routed_payload(top_scores, selected_experts):
+    """The folded payload the AutoEP layer builds for score_apply="post"."""
+    num_tokens, top_k = selected_experts.shape
+    token_indices_sorted = torch.argsort(selected_experts.reshape(-1), stable=True)
+    expert_indices = selected_experts.reshape(-1).index_select(0, token_indices_sorted)
+    no_assignments = torch.zeros_like(expert_indices, dtype=torch.bool)
+    payload = RoutedAssignmentPayload(
+        token_indices=token_indices_sorted // top_k,
+        expert_indices=expert_indices,
+        assignment_indices=assignment_ordinals_by_expert(expert_indices),
+        capacity_slots=token_indices_sorted % top_k,
+        combine_weights=top_scores.reshape(-1).index_select(0, token_indices_sorted),
+        drop_mask=no_assignments,
+        pad_mask=no_assignments.clone(),
+        input_splits=[expert_indices.numel()],
+        output_splits=[expert_indices.numel()],
+        extra={
+            "destination_ranks": torch.zeros_like(expert_indices),
+            "num_tokens": torch.tensor(num_tokens, dtype=torch.long),
+        },
+    )
+    return payload, token_indices_sorted
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _fused_restore_available(), reason="the fused weighted restore needs CUDA and Triton")
+class TestRestoreCombinedFusedTensorParallel(DistributedTest):
+    world_size = 2
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("row_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+    def test_matches_the_unpartitioned_fused_restore(self, row_dtype):
+        device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+        tp_group = dist.get_world_group()
+        tp_rank = dist.get_rank()
+        num_tokens, top_k, num_experts, hidden = 48, 4, 8, 130
+        generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(20261008)
+        router_logits = torch.rand(num_tokens, num_experts, device=device, generator=generator)
+        selected_experts = router_logits.argsort(dim=1)[:, :top_k]
+        top_scores = torch.rand(num_tokens, top_k, device=device, generator=generator)
+        rows = torch.randn(num_tokens * top_k, hidden, device=device, dtype=row_dtype, generator=generator)
+        # Multiples of 1/8, so adding the peers' upstream gradients is exact in every row dtype.
+        upstream = torch.randint(-4, 5, (num_tokens, hidden), device=device, generator=generator).to(row_dtype) / 8
+
+        actual_rows = rows.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        actual_scores = top_scores.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        payload, token_indices_sorted = _routed_payload(actual_scores, selected_experts)
+        _, ctx = partition_assignments(payload, tp_group=tp_group, tp_rank=tp_rank, tp_size=self.world_size)
+        # Odd per-expert counts give the peers different row counts, which the padded gather must handle.
+        rows_per_peer = torch.bincount(payload.assignment_indices % self.world_size, minlength=self.world_size)
+        assert rows_per_peer.unique().numel() > 1
+
+        restored = restore_combined_fused(actual_rows.index_select(0, ctx.local_indices),
+                                          ctx,
+                                          tp_group=tp_group,
+                                          top_k=top_k,
+                                          validate_coverage=True)
+        # Each peer back-propagates a different gradient through its replicated copy of the output.
+        restored.backward(upstream * (tp_rank + 1))
+
+        expected_rows = rows.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        expected_scores = top_scores.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        expected = fused_ops.fused_weighted_restore(expected_rows,
+                                                    top_scores=expected_scores,
+                                                    token_indices_sorted=token_indices_sorted,
